items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter and cryptic names run through the business logic: `c`, `k`, `lp`, `cp`, `lsz`, `csz`, `d0`, `r1`, `s0`, `lf`, `cf`. The vec.zig helpers do have doc comments, but the mask builders `int3Part`/`int4Part` are only lightly explained.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The process path in main.zig is one monolithic function holding both the horizontal pass and the vertical/output pass, well over 100 lines. kernels.zig is very likely over 500 lines. The diff also contains build artifacts (.zig-cache/h/*.txt, zig-out/lib/libswscale_candidate.so).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Missing planes are caught with `src_data[1] orelse return error.Bad`, so errors are not swallowed. Masks and pixel sizes are hard-coded numbers (e.g. `deint(4…)`/`store3` paths, `@setEvalBranchQuota(100000)`), and the fixed-point constants are not visible in the diff.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: Rows are addressed with `rowPtr(s, src_stride[i], y)` / `rowPtrM(d, dst_stride[i], y)` on every plane. Kernels run a `while (i + N <= w)` main loop followed by tails. About 2,000 random cases with odd and tiny sizes, all format pairs and all algorithms matched the reference.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: `nm -D --defined-only` shows only swscale_create, swscale_process and swscale_destroy. It links only libc, and objdump finds 0 zmm/k-register instructions. Kernels are chosen in create, the target is x86-64-v3 in build.zig, and nothing spawns threads.
